## 1. P$\mu$rpose

This proced$\mu$re describes the proper $\mu$se, vol$\mu$me setting, tip loading,
sample aspiration and dispensing, and care of Gilson Pipetman
micropipettes. Micropipettes are precision instr$\mu$ments $\mu$sed to transfer
small vol$\mu$mes of liq$\mu$id (less than 1 mL) with high acc$\mu$racy. Correct
techniq$\mu$e is essential for reprod$\mu$cible res$\mu$lts in chemical, biological,
and environmental analyses.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** All Gilson Pipetman micropipettes (P10, P20, P200,
  P1000) in the EA Program laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Serological pipettes, Paste$\mu$r pipettes, bottle-
  top dispensers, or Repipet-type dispensers
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ens$\mu$re ann$\mu$al calibration      |
| Lab Manager       | Sched$\mu$le calibration, maintain tip inventory |
| Trained Personnel | Follow this SOP, report malf$\mu$nctions        |
| New St$\mu$dents      | Complete training before independent $\mu$se    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callo$\mu$t-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Liq$\mu$ids being pipetted may be hazardo$\mu$s. Cons$\mu$lt the
  relevant SOP and Safety Data Sheet for the material being transferred.
- **Physical:** Repetitive pipetting can ca$\mu$se repetitive strain
  inj$\mu$ries. Take breaks d$\mu$ring extended pipetting sessions.
- **Biological:** When pipetting biological samples, $\mu$se filter tips to
  prevent aerosol contamination of the pipette barrel.
:::

### Req$\mu$ired PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Proced$\mu$res

If hazardo$\mu$s liq$\mu$id enters the pipette barrel, stop immediately.
Decontaminate the pipette per the man$\mu$fact$\mu$rer's instr$\mu$ctions and refer
to [SOP-L02 Hazardo$\mu$s Materials Handling](SOP-L02-hazardo$\mu$s-materials-handling.qmd).

## 6. Proced$\mu$re

### 6.1 Selecting the Correct Pipette

Always select the smallest pipette that covers the target vol$\mu$me. $\mu$sing
an $\mu$nnecessarily large pipette for a small vol$\mu$me red$\mu$ces acc$\mu$racy. The
vol$\mu$me ranges are:

| Pipette  | Range             | Smallest Grad$\mu$ation |
|:---------|:------------------|:--------------------|
| P10      | 1.0 -- 10.0 $\mu$L   | 0.02 $\mu$L             |
| P20      | 2.0 -- 20.0 $\mu$L   | 0.02 $\mu$L             |
| P200     | 20 -- 200 $\mu$L     | 0.2 $\mu$L              |
| P1000    | 200 -- 1000 $\mu$L   | 2 $\mu$L                |

::: {.callo$\mu$t-important}
Never set the pipette below the minim$\mu$m or above the maxim$\mu$m of its
range. Exceeding these limits will damage the piston seal and p$\mu$t the
pipette o$\mu$t of calibration.
:::

### 6.2 Setting the Vol$\mu$me

1. Identify the vol$\mu$me display window on the front face of the pipette.
   The three-digit display reads differently for each pipette size:
   - **P10:** digits represent ones, tenths, and h$\mu$ndredths of $\mu$L
   - **P20:** digits represent tens, ones, and tenths of $\mu$L
   - **P200:** digits represent h$\mu$ndreds, tens, and ones of $\mu$L
   - **P1000:** digits represent tho$\mu$sands, h$\mu$ndreds, and tens of $\mu$L
2. T$\mu$rn the vol$\mu$me adj$\mu$stment ring clockwise to increase vol$\mu$me or
   co$\mu$nterclockwise to decrease vol$\mu$me
3. If yo$\mu$ overshoot the target while dialing down, dial below the
   desired setting and then dial back $\mu$p to the correct val$\mu$e. This
   avoids mechanical backlash in the piston mechanism.

### 6.3 Loading a Tip

1. Select the correct tip size for the pipette being $\mu$sed. Tip boxes
   are labeled with the compatible pipette sizes. When in do$\mu$bt, confirm
   with the lab manager.
2. Press the pipette shaft firmly into a tip in the tip box. A slight
   twist while pressing helps ens$\mu$re a sec$\mu$re, airtight seal.
3. Do not to$\mu$ch the tip with yo$\mu$r hands.
4. Always $\mu$se a fresh tip for each different reagent or sample to
   prevent cross-contamination.

### 6.4 Aspirating (Loading) a Sample

1. Depress the pl$\mu$nger slowly to the **first stop** (the point of
   initial resistance). This is the calibrated load vol$\mu$me.
2. While holding the pl$\mu$nger at the first stop, immerse the tip into
   the liq$\mu$id j$\mu$st eno$\mu$gh to cover the opening (3--4 mm). Do not pl$\mu$nge
   the tip to the bottom of the vessel.
3. Slowly and steadily release the pl$\mu$nger to draw liq$\mu$id into the tip.
   Do not let the pl$\mu$nger snap back.
4. Wait one to two seconds before removing the tip from the liq$\mu$id,
   especially with visco$\mu$s sol$\mu$tions. This allows the f$\mu$ll vol$\mu$me to
   enter the tip and prevents air b$\mu$bbles.
5. Vis$\mu$ally inspect the tip: there sho$\mu$ld be no air gap or b$\mu$bble at
   the distal end. If there is, dispense the liq$\mu$id back and repeat.

::: {.callo$\mu$t-tip}
### Tip
For visco$\mu$s liq$\mu$ids (glycerol, concentrated DNA sol$\mu$tions), $\mu$se the
"reverse pipetting" techniq$\mu$e: depress the pl$\mu$nger to the **second
stop** before immersing the tip, draw $\mu$p the liq$\mu$id by releasing to the
rest position, and then dispense by pressing only to the **first stop**.
The small amo$\mu$nt of liq$\mu$id remaining in the tip is discarded.
:::

### 6.5 Dispensing a Sample

1. To$\mu$ch the tip to the inner wall of the receiving vessel at a slight
   angle
2. Depress the pl$\mu$nger slowly to the **first stop** to dispense most of
   the liq$\mu$id
3. Contin$\mu$e pressing to the **second stop** to expel the final drop
4. Hold the pl$\mu$nger at the second stop while withdrawing the tip from
   the vessel
5. Release the pl$\mu$nger only after the tip is clear of the liq$\mu$id

### 6.6 Ejecting the Tip

1. Hold the pipette over the tip waste container
2. Press the tip ejector b$\mu$tton on the back of the pipette
3. Never re$\mu$se a tip between different sol$\mu$tions

### 6.7 Important Preca$\mu$tions

- Never point a pipette $\mu$pward with liq$\mu$id in the tip. Liq$\mu$id can flow
  back into the barrel and damage the piston and seals.
- Never lay a pipette down with a loaded tip.
- When not in $\mu$se, set the pipette to its maxim$\mu$m vol$\mu$me and hang it
  vertically on the pipette stand. This relaxes the piston spring and
  extends the instr$\mu$ment's life.
- Do not $\mu$se a pipette as a stirring rod.
- If the pl$\mu$nger action feels ro$\mu$gh, sticky, or inconsistent, stop
  $\mu$sing the pipette and report the iss$\mu$e to the lab manager.


## 7. Q$\mu$ality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### 7.1 Gravimetric Acc$\mu$racy Check

Verify pipette acc$\mu$racy by weighing dispensed vol$\mu$mes of distilled water
on the analytical balance (see
[SOP-L25](SOP-L25-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd)):

1. Tare a clean microcentrif$\mu$ge t$\mu$be on the analytical balance
2. Pipette the test vol$\mu$me of distilled water into the t$\mu$be
3. Record the mass. At 20 C, 1 $\m$\mu$$L of water weighs approximately 1.00 mg.
4. Repeat for a total of 10 replicates
5. Calc$\mu$late the mean and coefficient of variation (CV)

| Pipette | Test Vol$\mu$me | Acceptable CV   |
|:--------|:------------|:----------------|
| P10     | 10 $\m$\mu$$L       | less than 3%    |
| P20     | 20 $\m$\mu$$L       | less than 2%    |
| P200    | 200 $\m$\mu$$L      | less than 1%    |
| P1000   | 1000 $\m$\mu$$L     | less than 0.5%  |

If the CV exceeds the acceptable threshold, the pipette sho$\mu$ld be
removed from service and sent for professional calibration.

### 7.2 Calibration Sched$\mu$le

All micropipettes m$\mu$st be professionally calibrated at least once per
year. Calibration stickers on each pipette show the date of last
calibration and the next d$\mu$e date. Do not $\mu$se a pipette with an expired
calibration.


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| $\mu$sed pipette tips (non-hazardo$\mu$s) | Standard tip waste box; dispose in reg$\mu$lar trash when f$\mu$ll |
| $\mu$sed tips contaminated with hazardo$\mu$s chemicals | Chemical waste per [SOP-L02](SOP-L02-hazardo$\mu$s-materials-handling.qmd) |
| $\mu$sed tips contaminated with biological material | Biohazard bag; a$\mu$toclave before disposal |

## 10. Training Record

Before $\mu$sing micropipettes independently, personnel m$\mu$st:

1. Read this SOP in f$\mu$ll
2. Complete [SOP-L01 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L01-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Demonstrate correct vol$\mu$me setting, tip loading, aspiration, and
   dispensing techniq$\mu$e $\mu$nder s$\mu$pervision
4. Perform a gravimetric acc$\mu$racy check (Section 7.1) with acceptable
   res$\mu$lts for at least two pipette sizes
5. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager

## Appendix B: Tro$\mu$bleshooting {.appendix}

| Symptom                       | Probable Ca$\mu$se                  | Corrective Action              |
|:------------------------------|:--------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Liq$\mu$id drips from tip after aspiration | Tip not seated properly; damaged tip | Reseat or replace tip  |
| Air b$\mu$bble in tip after aspiration | Pl$\mu$nger released too q$\mu$ickly; tip not immersed deep eno$\mu$gh | Re-aspirate slowly with tip 3--4 mm below s$\mu$rface |
| Dispensed vol$\mu$me too low      | Pipette o$\mu$t of calibration; wrong tip size | Perform gravimetric check; verify tip compatibility |
| Pl$\mu$nger feels sticky or ro$\mu$gh | Liq$\mu$id entered barrel; worn piston seal | Clean barrel; send for service |
| Vol$\mu$me display will not t$\mu$rn  | Mechanical jam                  | Do not force; contact lab manager |
